e.etymology: A spelling of Kit, the old short form of Christopher and of Katherine. Kitt is also an English and German surname.

assoc.t: KITT, the talking car in Knight Rider

e.etymology: A spelling of Ayansh, a modern Indian name ending in Sanskrit ansh, portion or part. It is usually explained as the first ray of light or as a part of one's parents.
A spelling of Cason or Kason, modern American names in the pattern of Mason and Jason, also influenced by Case and Casey.
A recent American coinage built on Eva or Evan, close in sound to Avani and Giovanni.
From the surname of Baltimore Orioles Hall of Famer Cal Ripken Jr., a family name of German origin.

assoc.t: Cal Ripken Jr., baseball's Iron Man

e.etymology: A stylized spelling of Mars, the planet and the Roman god of war, also used as a short form of names beginning Mar-. As a German surname, Marz comes from the month of March.
A short form of Timothy, from Greek Timotheos, honoring God.

e.meaning: from Brittany, the land of the Britons
e.etymology: A spelling of Brittany, the region of northwestern France settled by Britons, from Latin Britannia. It was one of the defining American girls' names of the late 1980s.
namesakes: Brittney Griner (WNBA star and Olympic gold medalist)

assoc.t: Brittney Griner, WNBA star jailed in Russia in 2022

e.etymology: From Old English wil, will, and heard, hardy or brave. It survived as a surname and returned to first-name use in America.
A spelling of Lacey, a Norman surname from the village of Lassy in Normandy, later linked with the fabric lace. Laci is also a Hungarian pet form of László.

assoc.t: Laci Peterson, California murder victim in 2002

e.etymology: A transposed spelling of Israel, long found in US birth records. Israel is the name given to Jacob in Genesis after he wrestles with the angel, read as he struggles with God.
e.note: Usually taken as a misspelling of Israel.

e.etymology: A name used by Hispanic American families, built on Mar-, as in Maria, with the -ely ending of Arely and Nayely.
A form of Rommel, a German and Dutch surname that became a given name in Latin America and the Philippines. In the United States it also sits beside Romell and Jamel.
A short form of Camilla, Emilia and Ludmila used in Finland and Scandinavia, and a spelling of the Slavic name Mila, dear or gracious.
namesakes: Milla Jovovich (actress in the Resident Evil films)

e.meaning: son of Hann, a medieval form of John
e.etymology: From the English surname meaning son of Hann, a medieval pet form of John. In America it also stands in for Scandinavian Hansen, son of Hans.

assoc.t: Hanson, the 1990s pop band behind MMMBop

e.etymology: A respelling of Ansley, an English place-name surname from Old English ansetl, hermitage, and leah, clearing. It is especially popular in the American South.
From Arabic adil, just or fair, from adl, justice.
A name used mainly by Mexican and Mexican American families, usually written Amairani. Its origin is not documented.

e.meaning: Zion; in Welsh, God is gracious
e.etymology: In the United States mostly a spelling of Zion, the hill of Jerusalem, as written in older Bibles. Siôn, said like Shawn, is the Welsh form of John, God is gracious.
From Turkish kayra, grace or benevolence, especially divine favor; in Turkic myth Kayra is also a creator god. In the United States it is also used as a spelling of Kyra or Kaira.
From an English place-name surname, Old English for the clearing of a man named Locc. Loxley in Yorkshire is the legendary home of Robin Hood, Robin of Loxley.

assoc.t: Robin of Loxley, another name for Robin Hood

e.etymology: A modern Indian name from Sanskrit ahan, day, taken to mean dawn or the first light of morning.
A recent American coinage that puts the -lee ending on Brix, as in Brixton, alongside Brinlee and Paislee.
A recent American coinage, said like the fabric suede and written in the style of Wade and Slade.
From Hebrew Dinah, judged or vindicated. In Genesis Dinah is the daughter of Jacob and Leah.
A pet form of Hugh, from the Germanic word hug, mind, heart or spirit, spelled the way Hughie sounds.
namesakes: Huey Lewis (singer of Huey Lewis and the News)
Huey P. Newton (Black Panther Party co-founder)

assoc.t: Huey, one of Donald Duck's three nephews

e.etymology: A spelling of Kendall, an English surname from the town of Kendal in Cumbria, the valley of the River Kent.
The Italian and Spanish form of Mireille, a name coined by the Provençal poet Frédéric Mistral for his 1859 poem Mirèio, from the Occitan verb mirar, to admire.
The Russian, Ukrainian and Bulgarian spelling of Maria, and the Arabic form used by Muslim families in South Asia. Maria is the Latin form of Hebrew Miriam, whose meaning is debated.
A spelling of Kendrick, a surname with several sources, among them the Old English name Cyneric, royal power, and the Welsh name Cynwrig.
A Mexican spelling of Noemí, the Spanish form of Naomi, from Hebrew for my pleasantness. The silent h marks the break between the vowels.
A spelling of Ronnie, the pet form of Ronald, from Old Norse Rognvaldr, ruler's counsel. This spelling is common in Latin America; Roni is also a Hebrew name meaning my joy.
